settings.title: Flat-Fee Nil T2 Filing for Cleaning Corporations

settings.editor:
Cleaning corporations wind down one contract at a time, which is why the last one tends to outlive the business. A single office still invoiced monthly makes the whole year an earning year. Where the contracts had genuinely all ended, the year is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Whether the staff were let go, the contracts went to another company, the work moved into a new corporation, or you clean a few houses in your own name now, the year is tested against what the corporation invoiced, anything a subcontractor was paid through it, and whether equipment left. Schedules 100, 125, 141 and 50 are prepared and the return is transmitted electronically. An invoicing year goes to the full service.

What keeps these corporations alive is usually the hope of bidding again, or an open payroll account nobody has closed. Each year of waiting is a tax year with a return behind it.

A year with nothing invoiced is $300.00 plus HST per tax year. Outstanding years are worked as a set from the earliest forward so each opening balance agrees with the one before.

settings.title: Which T2 Schedules a Cleaning Corporation Files

settings.editor:
ScheduleWhat it reportsOn a nil yearWhy
Schedule 100Balance sheet informationRequiredMachines and vacuums, supplies still in a store room, any amount owing to a shareholder and retained profit all sit here.
Schedule 125Income statement informationRequiredContract revenue nil, wages nil, which is what a year without a live site reports.
Schedule 141Notes checklistRequiredFiled with the two GIFI schedules and records who assembled them.
Schedule 50Shareholder informationRequiredHolders of 10% or more, commonly a husband and wife who ran the rounds themselves.
Schedule 24First-time filer informationFirst return onlyRequired on the first return the corporation ever files, and on no other.
Schedule 8Capital cost allowanceOnly where equipment is heldFloor machines, a pressure washer and a van are depreciable property. A corporation with only mops and buckets may have none.

Source: the Canada Revenue Agency, on what accompanies a T2, measured against a cleaning corporation holding no live contract. Reviewed 23 November 2026.

settings.html:
The year is nil

  • Not one contract or one-off clean was invoiced by the corporation
  • No subcontract cleaner was paid through it
  • No equipment, van or machine belonging to it was sold
  • No supplies were sold on to another operator
  • No interest was credited to it during the year

The year is not nil

  • A site was invoiced, even for a single month
  • A one-off or move-out clean was billed by it
  • A machine, a van or a floor polisher was disposed of
  • Leftover supplies were sold to another cleaning company
  • A client list or contract was transferred for value

Due either way

  • There is a return for each tax year the corporation stays registered
  • There is a T183CORP behind each of those returns before it moves
  • There is Schedule 50 disclosure once a holding reaches 10%
  • There are payroll and sales tax accounts running on their own cycles
  • There is a clearance certificate to get before dissolving

settings.title: Cleaning Corporation Filing Across Canada

settings.editor:
Cleaning corporations are filed the same way wherever the registered office sits, because the return is prepared and transmitted electronically from end to end. There is nothing to print, nothing to post and nothing to sign in person.

Where the corporation was incorporated changes the registry, not the return. An Ontario corporation answers to the Ontario Business Registry, and corporations in British Columbia, Alberta, Quebec and Saskatchewan each answer to their own. The T2 itself is federal and identical in all of them. Within Ontario, a corporation registered in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton or Ottawa is filed on the same terms and at the same price as one anywhere else in the country.

Two provinces add a return the federal T2 does not cover. A Quebec corporation also files the CO-17 and an Alberta corporation also files the AT1. Both are separate provincial returns, and neither is included in the $300.00 plus HST fee.
